TVL stands for Total Value Locked. It’s a key metric used primarily in the decentralized finance (DeFi) space to measure the total value of assets—usually cryptocurrencies—that are currently being staked, lent, or otherwise locked into a particular protocol or smart contract. TVL gives an indication of the amount of capital users have committed to that protocol, which can help gauge its popularity, trustworthiness, and liquidity. For example, a DeFi lending platform with a high TVL means a lot of users have deposited assets there, making it potentially more robust and liquid.

TVL is typically expressed in terms of a fiat currency equivalent (like USD) to provide an easy-to-understand valuation. It’s commonly used when comparing different protocols across blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, or others, to see which ones have more value locked and are potentially more influential in the ecosystem.
